newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bonds seen fuelling Madrid stocks despite earnings.
newsitem.headline: Bonds seen fuelling Madrid stocks despite earnings.

text.p: Madrid stocks are set for a rally of up to 10 percent in the IBEX index of 35 leading shares over the next six months fueled by bond gains amid expectations for new rate cuts, analysts said on Thursday.
The outlook for further interest rate cuts will allow investors to temporarily ignore weaker earnings expected for both this year and next.

"We're pretty bullish at the moment, mainly because while bonds are still strong they support stocks. Despite the fact that earnings this year will be weak and for the next two years they won't be marvellous, this should underpin stocks," said a trader at a Madrid brokerage.
She said this could power the Ibex to around 4,670 in the next six months, up around 10 percent from current levels as investors focus on index funds.
Some expect further rate cuts to fuel bonds to new highs, even after the Bank of Spain lopped 50 basis points off its key money rate today, leaving it at 6.75 percent.
"We could see a further 50 basis point cut before the end of the year," the trader said.
Bond strength combined with this more cautious corporate earnings outlook means interest in the bourse will be focused on the Ibex-35 index itself rather than individual companies, the trader said.
Earnings doubts are focused on lower than expected increases in regulated tariffs, deregulation and a relatively weak economy, analysts said.
But some are more skeptical on the scope for further monetary easing.

"The Bank of Spain has to keep its eye on the inflation ball if it wants to hit the Maastricht criteria. (It) may be more reluctant to provide rate cut support than it has been in the past. But it's not out of the question," Credit Suisse First Boston equities strategist David Aserkoff said.
Nevertheless lower interest rates and bond gains so far could provide more fuel for stocks, he said.
"We've got good interest rates on the one hand and lousy earnings on the other. But interest rates might well win over," he said.

Aserkoff saw value in selected stocks, banking group Argentaria, electricity giant Endesa and Telefonica whose earnings could prove more resilient, or whose yield looks more attractive as bond yields come down.
